title: LCARS Capability Profile
description: Structural schema for a composed Capability Profile. Semantic invariants (enums, value constraints) are checked by Fleet.CapProfile.validate/1 (G24). STRICT: additionalProperties:false at every object level — an unknown/typo'd field (e.g. `containmnet`) is REJECTED, not silently ignored (R0-CAP-001). As the COMPOSED profile (base + modops) is validated here, this also catches junk fields introduced by a modop fragment (R0-CAP-009 backstop).

network.description: Ce que le pod peut joindre. Absent = `vendor-only` (fail-closed) : la sortie passe par le proxy CONNECT du pod, dont l'allowlist est la declaration d'endpoints du vendor et rien d'autre. `egress` ajoute les hotes declares par le role. Un pod n'a JAMAIS de namespace reseau : le choix porte sur l'allowlist, pas sur l'ouverture.

forge_identity.description: Does this role hold a forge identity (account + role token)? Absent = true. The four-list equality check (roles.provisioning_locked, BL-6-45) counts only forge_identity roles against forge.tf/ROLES/PROV_ROLES. false is the EXPLICIT declaration of the asymmetry (starfleet: an orchestrator whose forge writes all go through the system account).

mounts.description: CATALOGUE mounts projected into the bwrap sandbox — ONE OF THE TWO DECLARATIVE SURFACES, and the per-role one. bwrap_launch binds them at the SAME path, RO/RW, after the /home tmpfs. Inert when containment: none (host = native access). Empty/absent here means no extra CATALOGUE mount, never a bare pod: a pod's world is composed from five sources, and the other three are deliberately NOT here. Declarative: this list (per role) and the spawn call's `mounts:` opt (per call). RUNTIME INVARIANTS, in code precisely because a catalogue is SUBSTITUTABLE and an invariant an operator can replace does not constrain: the launcher's own directory (a pod that cannot exec its launcher is not a pod), the project's ops worktree, and the code worktree as a read-only reference for a producer working the other face. Do not migrate those three here — moving a rule into a file an operator brings makes it a setting. PRECEDENCE IS THE CONCATENATION ORDER, first occurrence of a path wins (`Enum.uniq_by`), and what it decides is a MODE: two sources naming one path resolve to the EARLIER one's ro/rw. So an audit of what a pod may write reads this list AND the order.

scope.$comment: allowedTools AND disallowedTools are HARD-REQUIRED by bin/claude_launch.sh (`jq -r '.spec.scope.<field> | join(",")' || exit 1` — an absent field makes `join` hit null, jq fails, the pod NEVER launches). A profile that would crash the launcher is rejected at LOAD time, not at spawn.

allowedTools.description: The role's declared MCP/native tool surface — ONE OF THE TWO GRANTING MECHANISMS, and the per-role one. NOT THE WHOLE SURFACE, and reading it as such is the trap: `claude_launch.sh` APPENDS `mcp__fleet__get_work_item` and `mcp__fleet__submit_result` to every pod, unconditionally, because the fleet work-item protocol is universal — a pod that cannot pull its order or return its result is not a pod. That pair is a RUNTIME INVARIANT and belongs in the launcher precisely because a catalogue is SUBSTITUTABLE: an operator bringing their own profiles must not be able to produce a pod that cannot answer. Do not migrate it here, and do not list it here either — a line that restates an invariant reads as the thing that grants it, and the next reader removes it. ⚠ THE CONVERSE IS NOT TRUE: this list DECLARES a surface, the vendor CONSTRUCTS it. A tool absent here is not thereby unreachable; `disallowedTools` in particular has been measured not to remove what is served to the model. So this field answers "what did we ask for", never "what can this pod do".

egress_hosts.description: LES HOTES QUE CE ROLE PEUT JOINDRE EN PLUS DE CEUX DE SON VENDOR — et rien tant que `metadata.network` ne vaut pas `egress`. `Fleet.Spawner.Pod.Egress.allowlist/2` compose `Vendor.hosts/1` (base obligatoire, lue a cote du launcher) PUIS cette liste, et seulement si le profil declare `network: egress`. Deux clefs, aucune ne suffit : `network` dit QUI a le droit de sortir, cette liste dit OU. ⚠ CETTE CLEF ETAIT LUE PAR LE CODE ET INTERDITE PAR CE SCHEMA. `role_hosts/1` fait `get_in(["scope", "egress_hosts"])` depuis son ecriture, alors que `scope` est en `additionalProperties: false` : aucun profil ne pouvait la porter, donc la moitie `role` de l'allowlist etait du code mort. Mesure 2026-08-19 : zero occurrence dans tout `runtime/priv`. Ajoutee ici pour que la declaration redevienne possible. UN HOTE PAR ENTREE, nom exact ou regle de sous-domaine `*.` ancree a droite — jamais un `contains`, jamais un suffixe nu : c'est l'ancre qui empeche `x.io.attaquant.net` de passer `*.x.io` (`Egress.decide/2`). Ni schema, ni port, ni chemin : le proxy ne decide que du HOTE.

sp_template.description: SP template used to materialize a PERMANENT pod (monk, archivist). Distinct from invocation.subagent_template, which implies a one-shot dispatch (G24-11).

remote_control.description: Claude Desktop visibility: false makes the launcher omit --remote-control (pod functional but invisible). Default (absent) = true. Set false on ephemeral judges (qualifier/reviewer).

wake_send_keys.description: Send-keys wake fallback authorized for this pod. Default (absent) = true. false = flag-only: the kick loop never types into the pod's terminal (set on the architect - interactive human session); the no-ACK wake.failed escalation remains the terminal net.

permission_mode.description: Claude CLI permission mode per role (catalogue chantier L2, B-06 2026-07-20 — the reader existed in Pod.LaunchSpec but the schema rejected the field, so it always fell to `default`). Absent = `default` (allow/deny lists ENFORCED). `bypassPermissions` re-opens yolo explicitly. Write enforcement is the MOUNT (RO/RW), not this — a judge keeps Write/Edit for its report, bounded by the mount.

slot_scope.description: POD IDENTITY GRANULARITY — optional. Absent => DERIVED from lifetime_scope (one-shot => instance, context-long => project), the historical rule. Explicit => wins. Exists because the derivation makes ONE combination inexpressible: context-long AND one pod per ticket (an engineer that survives its rework rounds but does not outlive its ticket).

output_compression.description: INERT TODAY — declaring this changes nothing, in either direction: the composed verdict (LaunchSpec.output_compression?/1) reaches no launch, because the token-saver hook rides a PreToolUse tier a pod CANNOT load — the sanctuary mounts only plugins/ and skills/, pod_settings_json/1 writes no hooks key, and the human .claude is excluded BECAUSE of its hooks. No carrier was ever lost: the v1 one targeted the user tier that --setting-sources excludes unconditionally, so it would never have fired either (measured 2026-08-07). The brick itself IS shipped and tested; wiring it means INVENTING a vehicle in a sanctuary designed to mount none — a feature with a design decision behind it, not a fix. See vendor/token_saver/VENDOR.md. INTENDED semantics, kept so the field means the same thing the day it is wired: compress this role's Bash output before it enters the agent's context. Default (absent) = true. Set false where the FULL output is the work: a judge reading a diff, a debug run. Composed with the fleet knob by an AND — the fleet may only CUT compression, never force it on a role that declared false, because compression LOSES information and the safe direction is toward less of it.

response_sec.description: Per-role watchdog: max seconds of silence on the pod's active task before the result-deadline fires (catalogue chantier L2, B-06 2026-07-20 — the reader existed in Pod.Liveness but the schema rejected `timeouts`). Absent = a scope-coded default (one-shot 300 s; forever inert). INTEGER only (a float would crash the deadline arm).

capabilities.description: Business RESPONSIBILITIES the role carries (catalogue chantier L3, B-03 2026-07-20). The gates resolve a CAPABILITY via CapProfile.has_capability?, NEVER a magic role name. `onboarder` = may enrol and retire projects (create/import/open/adopt/close/revise) — a PREDICATE on the pod that knocks, so any number of carriers is legitimate and nothing resolves 'the onboarder'; `project_delegate` = delegates issues within its own project — EXACTLY ONE, it is ensured per repo and named by no card; `exception_judge` = the soft-gate escalation judge AND the signatory of the seal — EXACTLY ONE, two signatories is an ambiguity about who signs; `conflict_resolver` = handed a merge conflict the producer could not resolve — EXACTLY ONE, and a SEPARATE key from exception_judge on purpose, so substituting the resolver never moves the seal's signature; `producer` = produces the deliverable — AT LEAST ONE, several is a normal specialised catalogue since each card names which one it dispatches. Which role carries which is the CATALOGUE's business and is deliberately not stated here: an inventory in a contract is false for every catalogue but the one it was written from. Renaming/substituting a role = a cap-profile edit, not Elixir. Absent = no special responsibility.

project.description: THE CATALOGUE HALF ONLY, and the slot carries two populations. What a card may declare is listed here and validated (additionalProperties: false). The pilot then INJECTS repo, base_sha, gate_base_sha and pr_base_branch at dispatch through Fleet.CapProfile.with_project/2, which does not re-validate — they are read by live code and are absent here BY DESIGN, since a card that set base_sha would validate and then be overwritten at every dispatch, i.e. a knob that reads as configuration and does nothing. Single source of the runtime half: Fleet.CapProfile.runtime_project_keys/0, held against this list by mix lcars.contracts.check.

deliverable_mode.description: Shape of the role's deliverable, entry condition of Fleet.Workflow.Deliverable.publish/1 (differentiation by catalogue, not by code branch). `payload`: the pod produces a file payload, the SYSTEM writes+commits (verdict roles). `git_native`: the pod commits itself in its workspace, the system verifies (I-CBC gate) then pushes (code roles). Absent: the `payload` default is applied code-side (only relevant to steps with post_extract.git). OPTIONAL-with-default is DELIBERATE, the inverse of its dual `brief_kind` (REQUIRED): a wrong `payload` default is fail-SAFE (`StepRunConsumer.default_deliverable_mode` treats an unresolved role as `payload` = NON-producer, so its output is NEVER pushed as unverified code; only an EXPLICIT `git_native` enters the I-CBC gate), while a wrong `brief_kind` default (`worker`) would be fail-OPEN (a judge would execute attacking content) — hence `brief_kind` required and `deliverable_mode` not. Only the producer (engineer) declares `git_native`; judges/system omit it = correct `payload` default.

brief_kind.description: Shape of the BRIEF the role receives — entry dual of deliverable_mode (differentiation by catalogue, not by magic code name). `worker`: brief = executable instruction (the issue body); the role ACTS. `judge`: the role JUDGES and receives a defused I-CBC GateBrief (context + deliverable + verdict contract, NO executable instruction). REQUIRED (`spec.required`): judge-ness is a SECURITY property, NEVER inferred — a profile without `brief_kind` is REJECTED at load. No silent `worker` default (a judge missing `judge` would fall back to worker=execute = fail-open on attacking content).

systemPrompt.description: Name of ANOTHER catalogue role whose SP this role reuses, INSTEAD of owning an `agent-<name>-base.md` of its own. Absent (the normal case) = this role owns its draft, and having neither is refused: a role's cap-profile grants PERMISSIONS, its SP decides BEHAVIOUR, so a role with no prompt of its own behaves like whoever's prompt it inherited and its name lies. The one case this exists for is RENAMING: a catalogue that renames `architect` to something in its own language declares the new name here with `systemPrompt: architect` and reuses the validated prompt, instead of copying 200 lines that then drift. A ROLE NAME and not a path — the reuse is stated in the vocabulary of the catalogue, and there is no path to sanitise, escape or resolve. Reuse must be DECLARED: a silent fallback to a generic prompt is the trap this whole no-fallback doctrine removed.

interlocutor.description: Who this role's REPL converses with — the axis that decides which protocol contract is injected into `.lcars/protocole-user.md`. `fleet`: the fleet alone (engineer, judges) — machine protocol only, `engage` starts a work-item cycle and there is nobody to answer. `both`: the fleet AND a human at the same terminal (architect, starfleet) — machine protocol PLUS the human addendum; a pod the machine kicks and a human also talks to. `human`: a human alone — no work-item rail, no `engage`; the human is the source of work. REQUIRED (`spec.required`), NEVER inferred: an unstated interlocutor was silently `fleet` for every pod ever spawned, which is why an interactive architect was being served a protocol saying `SeeU` closes nothing and no handoff exists. Three values and not a human/machine boolean, because feeding and facing are INDEPENDENT and the architect proves it (machine-kicked via wake_send_keys AND human-facing via the bridge); the fourth cell — fed by a human, nobody in front — has no referent and is unrepresentable by construction.

allOf.$comment: G24-10 : boot_at_start: true requires lifetime_scope: forever
G24-11 : subagent_template != null requires lifetime_scope: one-shot
G24-12 : host_native: true requires containment: none
